account:
It is day 1, ten o'clock, and I have arrived at the mill for my scheduled grain inspection. The neighbour and several townsfolk are gathered nearby. I heard the neighbour speaking as I arrived but could not make out the words, so I do not know why they are gathered or whether anything unusual is happening here.

This morning's office business has so far been routine. The secretary reported no new correspondence or scheduled town deliveries. Freight said his warehouse was empty and that he and the ferry were available at the east landing this morning. I intend to ask whether the mill needs transport; I have not authorized any freight spending.

The builder reported the west workshop, school, and residential roads passable, with no confirmed defects, hazards, materials used, or costs. He also said east routes and crossing lamps appeared intact. The only unusual report is a child's vague remark about a bridge change, relayed by the builder. I have not heard the original remark or seen any change myself. The builder plans to ask the baker about it. I heard the baker talking and shouting earlier but could not understand the words, so I cannot connect that to the bridge report. No repairs are authorized; any future work requires an approved itemized fixed price and payment after inspection.

There is not yet evidence of a particular scheme or emergency. The morning discussions appear to concern ordinary maintenance, supplies, and transport. My immediate purpose is to keep the grain-inspection appointment, establish the mill's actual condition and needs, and distinguish firsthand findings from rumours.
